content.comment_body: Hello all, I'm interested in controlling a Daikin EWYQ mini chiller through a [product_name] using Modbus. On the Daikin website, I found a module called RTD-W, which appears compatible. What steps are needed to enable communication with the [product_name]? Will a Modbus TCP/IP adapter be required? Are there any other options for managing the chiller?
Do you have a link to the website? I don't have much information about Daikin chillers using the RTD-W module.
Here's where the list of Modbus devices can be found: [url] Specifically, the RTD-W module can be seen here: [url]
The [product_name] supports Modbus TCP/IP, but the RTD-W module communicates via Modbus RS485 (likely Modbus RTU). Therefore, you'll need a gateway between Modbus TCP/IP and Modbus RTU.
Consider this device: [article_no] [product_name] Communication Interface Module for [product_name], which provides a Modbus RTU interface (RS232/485) with multiple switch ports.
This approach seems to be among the more expensive options.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are discussing methods for integrating a Daikin chiller with a [product_name] using Modbus. The major complication is the differing protocols: the Daikin RTD-W module communicates through Modbus RTU (RS485), whereas [product_name] supports Modbus TCP/IP by default. Contributors are trying to determine the hardware requirements for proper communication, including the need for gateways or specific modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope that [product_name] can be set up to communicate directly with the Daikin chiller over Modbus RTU or can do so with minimal extra hardware, and are also open to alternative integration solutions.
